assessments.reasoning: The pinned Python 3.13.0 Simple statements reference at lines 1009–1023 defines enclosing function-local scopes, chooses the nearest binding, and specifies SyntaxError for a missing binding. It also covers the distinct syntax error for using or assigning a name before the declaration in that scope.

The pinned Execution model at lines 103–116 and 136–156 defines lexical visibility, an intervening global declaration, and compile-time SyntaxError for absent nonlocal bindings. Its annotation scope text at lines 188–226 covers type parameters. The nearby whole-block binding rule at lines 127–132 explains why a lexical binding can exist independently of an assigned runtime value.

challenge.method: Compared both exact Python 3.13.0 sections and ran python-controls.py with CPython 3.13.5. Challenged nearest and unreachable local assignments, a module global alone, an intervening global, a class namespace, a type parameter, and the excluded __class__ closure.
challenge.results: An unreachable assignment still supplied the nearest local cell, which the inner function rebound independently of the outer name. Module-only, intervening-global, ordinary class-attribute, and type-parameter controls raised compile-time SyntaxError. The excluded __class__ closure returned the defining class.

limitations: The execution controls used CPython 3.13.5. The claim is about the exact pinned Python 3.13.0 reference.
